patterns.usage_note: A stiff, written dismissal: the action named is not worth the trouble, so the thing is beneath notice. It is the negative of 〜に足る／に足りる ('worthy of') — 足りる the modern ichidan verb, 足る the older godan one, so に足らない reads more classical — and it is heavily idiomatic, clustering around 取る, 驚く, 恐れる and 信頼する rather than being used freely; it also attaches to a bare noun (信頼に足りない, 恐れるに足らぬ相手), though the verb-plus-に shape is by far the commoner one. The は is optional and emphatic (驚くには足りない); note that with a plain noun subject 〜には足りない usually reads as plain insufficiency ('not enough for'), so the 'not worth' sense lives on the verb-plus-に(は)足りない frame.

examples.ruby: 根[ね]も葉[は]もない噂[うわさ]など、取[と]り上[あ]げるに足[た]りない。
examples.english: A groundless rumor like that isn't worth dignifying with attention.

examples.ruby: この程度[ていど]の失敗[しっぱい]は、何[なん]ら驚[おどろ]くに足[た]りない。
examples.english: A slip on this scale is nothing to be surprised at.

examples.ruby: あの証言[しょうげん]は矛盾[むじゅん]だらけで、信頼[しんらい]するに足[た]りない。
examples.english: That testimony is riddled with contradictions and deserves no trust.

patterns.usage_note: Rhetorical (反語) だい: question in form, flat denial in force. It is triggered by 何が or どこが plus the very label the speaker rejects — 何が名医だい means 'he is no great doctor', not a request for information — and the intonation falls instead of rising. Keep it apart from its two homophone siblings: the plain wh-question だい (l2 2521, 誰だい, いつだい) genuinely asks and takes 誰／いつ／どこへ, while the assertive だい (l2 2523, 嘘だい) makes a bare statement with no question word at all. Like them it is だ plus the emphatic 終助詞 い, so it sits on a noun (a verb needs explanatory ん first: 何が面白いんだい), and it is brusque, masculine, mostly fiction dialogue and hot-tempered speech.

examples.ruby: 何[なに]が名医[めいい]だい、風邪[かぜ]一[ひと]つ治[なお]せないくせに。
examples.english: Some great doctor — he can't even cure a cold.

examples.ruby: どこが親友[しんゆう]だい、困[こま]った時[とき]に知[し]らんぷりして。
examples.english: Best friend, my foot — you look the other way the moment I'm in trouble.

examples.ruby: この絵[え]の何[なに]が傑作[けっさく]だい、ただの落書[らくが]きだ。
examples.english: What's supposed to be a masterpiece about this painting? It's a scribble.

patterns.usage_note: A question aimed as much at oneself as at the listener, so it turns a claim into open musing; でしょうか is its polite twin and doubles as a deferential way to put a question to someone else. Around an obvious answer it works rhetorically and amounts to a flat denial (そんなことがあるだろうか), while 〜ないだろうか adds a hopeful tilt ('might it not be …?'). It attaches straight to plain forms, and after a noun or na-adjective no だ intervenes.

examples.ruby: この雨[あめ]の中[なか]、山[やま]の上[うえ]まで歩[ある]いて行[い]けるだろうか。
examples.english: In rain like this, I wonder if we can make it up the mountain on foot.

examples.ruby: この値段[ねだん]で、はたして人[ひと]が集[あつ]まるだろうか。
examples.english: At this price, I wonder if anyone will actually turn up.

examples.ruby: あのとき断[ことわ]ったのは、間違[まちが]いだっただろうか。
examples.english: Was turning it down back then a mistake, I wonder?
